name: LinkedIn Optimizer
tagline: Android app that scores and rewrites your LinkedIn headline, about section, and experience bullets.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a prompt wrapper with a scoring rubric on top, delivered as an Android app. There is no LinkedIn API involved here: you paste your own profile text in, the model rewrites it, you paste it back. An agent can reproduce the entire loop in a single session, including the keyword suggestions and the before/after diff, and you get to tune the rubric to your own industry instead of accepting someone else's. What you give up is the phone-shaped convenience and whatever prompt tuning the developer did by hand. If you already pay for an LLM key, the marginal cost of the DIY version is effectively zero.
coreLoopDIY: Paste your headline, about section, and experience bullets into a local web form, get a rubric score per section plus three rewrite variants and a keyword gap list, then copy the winner back to LinkedIn.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic) in .env
Your profile text, copied manually from LinkedIn
whatYouLose: A real mobile app you can poke at on the bus instead of a localhost tab
Whatever hand-tuning the developer baked into the prompts after seeing thousands of profiles
Any sense of what actually performs on LinkedIn right now, since neither version has data on that
Built-in example profiles and role-specific templates, unless you write your own
Updates when LinkedIn changes its character limits or section structure
moatNotes: The only real asset is prompt craft and app packaging, and prompt craft copies in one paste.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a few dollars on the Play Store is cheaper than an evening of setup, and because most people job hunting do not want to think about API keys. There is also a genuine packaging value: a single-purpose app with the right questions pre-asked beats a blank chat window for people who do not know what to ask for. That is real, it is just not defensible.
notes: A rubric plus a prompt plus a copy button, which is a perfectly honest product and also a perfectly easy afternoon.
prompt:
Build a local-only LinkedIn profile rewriting tool. Stack: Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, no database, no auth, no telemetry.

Structure:
- One page at /, client-side state only. Nothing persists except localStorage.
- Textareas for: Headline (220 char limit shown), About (2600 char limit shown), and a repeatable Experience Entry block with title, company, and bullet points.
- Inputs for Target Role and Target Industry, plus an optional paste box for a job description to align against.

API route at /api/review that calls the Anthropic Messages API with the key from process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Read it from .env.local, never hardcode it, include a .env.example.

The route takes the profile sections and returns strict JSON: per-section score out of 10 across four named criteria (specificity, keyword coverage, outcome orientation, readability), a one-line critique per criterion, three rewrite variants per section with distinct angles (metrics-forward, narrative, keyword-dense), and a keyword gap list comparing the profile against the target role or pasted job description. Validate the JSON with zod and retry once on parse failure.

UI: score cards with the criteria breakdown, rewrite variants side by side with a copy button each, character counts that turn red past the LinkedIn limit, and a plain-text diff view toggle between the original and the selected variant.

Export: a single button that downloads the whole reviewed profile as Markdown.

Explicitly out of scope: LinkedIn OAuth, scraping, auto-posting, accounts, hosting, analytics, payment. Do not add them.

Ship a README with setup in four steps and a hardcoded sample profile seeded behind a "Load example" button so the app is testable without typing.
